_comment: Mine art sources. Both mines — the overworld Mine and the badlands Company
Mine — were drawn entirely in flat fillRect colours. The Miner's Cave pack
ships a 32x32 master tileset at exactly the game's tile size, so this maps
its cells onto the TL mine enum and drawMineTile draws real art.
The source is one uniform grid, so cells are addressed as [col, row].
IMPORTANT — the pack draws several things as autotile RINGS: a 3x3 block of
cells whose middle is empty and whose eight edges are the border of an
opening. The rock wall ([0,0]-[2,2]), the boarded timber wall ([0,6]-[2,8])
and the rail loop ([0,24]-[2,26]) are all rings. Their cells are named here
by WHICH SIDE IS OPEN — wallOpenS is the piece to use for a wall tile with
floor to its south — so the dressing pass can pick the right one per tile
instead of scattering ring fragments around as if they were props.
`tiles` are single 32x32 cells drawn at the tile's top-left with no anchor.
`sprites` span stacked cells and anchor bottom-centre, so the thing stands on
its tile and overhangs upward. A minecart, a loaded ore cart and the timber
tunnel mouth are all 32x64 and were previously cut in half by being listed
as tiles.
The ore* groups and the seven loaded ore carts come from the same seven
columns of the sheet, so MINE_ORE_INDEX can park a cart of gold beside a
gold vein. Column 5, the cyan one, matches no vein the game has.
Run tools/build_mine.py after editing.
floor deliberately excludes cell [3,2]: it is the pack's flat untextured
fill, and mixed in with the cobble it read as pale mauve patches.
The pack also ships lava pools, water pools, coffins and a dragon trap. None
of those belong in a frontier coal mine, so none of them are mapped.

oreCoal._: The pack has no black ore, and coal that is not black is not coal.
